reason: Moodle-recorded time in the LMS is correlated with course points (r = 0.75, all 208; r = 0.46, active participants). Meets I1. Blind I also listed I2, but 'external motivation' is a credit incentive for one subgroup, not a measured construct. Borderline E3: only 44 of 208 are university students.

extraction_check.n_quote: 208 students enrolled on this given course, in the following composition: 79% (165) female and 21% (43) male students

effect_sizes.value: r = 0.75 (time spent in LMS ↔ course achievement (points), whole sample)
effect_sizes.quote: between the amount of time spent in the LMS and student achievements - amount of acquired points (Pearson correlation factor r= 0.75, p= 0.001).

effect_sizes.value: r = 0.46 (time spent in LMS ↔ course achievement, active students only)
effect_sizes.quote: the amount of time spent in the LMS and the variable of student achievements show a significant correlation (Pearson correlation factor = 0.46, p=0.001).

effect_sizes.value: r = 0.38 (external motivation ↔ time spent in LMS)
effect_sizes.quote: External motivation and the variable of time spent in this framework demonstrated an apparent relationship (Pearson correlation factor=0.38, p=0.001).

effect_sizes.value: r = 0.25 (external motivation ↔ time spent in LMS, students who logged in)
effect_sizes.quote: a statistically outstanding correlation emerges between the external motivation and time spent in LMS (Pearson correlation factor = 0.25, p= 0.003).

table2_row.country: Serbia and Hungary (MOOC participants: 135 Serbia, 71 Hungary, 2 Romania)
table2_row.design: correlational case study (Pearson r, t-tests, ANOVA)
table2_row.lms_indicators: time spent in the Moodle LMS (system-recorded)
table2_row.outcome_or_construct: course achievement (points from assignments, forum, final test); 'external motivation' (receiving formal-course credit, self-reported at application)
table2_row.effect_size: r = 0.75 (time in LMS vs course points, n = 208); r = 0.46 (active participants only)

table2_row_source: assessor extraction, cells confirmed by adjudicator
borderline: E3: MOOC sample of 99 'students' (the primary target group is secondary-school students), 86 teachers and 23 others; 44 are university students. Mixed, so not a clearly non-HE sample; included with this caveat.
